finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Connection-pool exhaustion from per-instance Prisma clients
File: src/lib/db.ts (L1-L220) and src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L60)
Evidence: Module-level code constructs a new PrismaClient in production (createPrismaClient called when NODE_ENV === "production") while the global singleton pattern is only applied in non-production, so each serverless instance/cold start creates a separate Prisma client (and its DB pool). This repository uses Postgres via Prisma (prisma/schema.prisma).
Impact: On serverless hosts (Vercel/Next) many cold-started instances × Prisma's per-client connection pool (~10) will exhaust Postgres connections and spike DB CPU/IOPS; expect failures ~tens of concurrent cold starts (~10–50 requests) depending on DB max_connections. Break mode: connection pool exhaustion and elevated DB latency.
Fix: Always reuse a single PrismaClient across lambda instances (assign to globalThis in all environments) and introduce a proper pooler (PgBouncer / serverless pool) or reduce per-client pool size + use pgbouncer.

[DB-2] Checkout/payment flow writes not atomic (financial inconsistency risk)
File: src/app/api/checkout/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: The route does db.user.findUnique -> maybe db.user.create, then calls stripe.customers.create, then performs db.user.update to store stripeCustomerId — no db.$transaction, no idempotency or upsert handling for concurrent requests. External Stripe call is not guarded by a DB transaction/compensating logic.
Impact: Under concurrent or failing DB conditions this yields partial success (Stripe customer created but DB not updated) or race-created duplicate errors; at scale this causes billing / customer-mapping inconsistencies and manual reconciliation (break mode: data inconsistency and failed checkout flows under ~>10x QPS with retries).
Fix: Make DB writes idempotent and atomic: use upsert or wrap related DB mutations in a transaction, add idempotency keys for external Stripe calls, and persist mapping only after consistent local writes or implement compensating rollback logic.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-3] Unbounded room list query (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/fetch_all_rooms/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: Handler calls db.room.findMany() with no where/take/skip/cursor or guard, returning all rows.
Impact: A full table scan and huge payloads will blow up DB CPU/IOPS and application latency as rooms grow; under 10x QPS this will cause long-running queries and high memory/network usage.
Fix: Add cursor-based pagination or hard limits (take/skip or cursor), enforce auth/authorization, and avoid returning whole rows (select only required columns).

[DB-4] Missing index on Room.hostId used in queries
File: prisma/schema.prisma (Room model region, roughly L120-L200)
Evidence: Room model defines hostId and mapId relations but there is no @@index on hostId (queries use where: { hostId: userId } in fetch_rooms).
Impact: Queries filtering by hostId will perform sequential scans as the rooms table grows, increasing latency and DB CPU; at scale this causes first-order slowdown for any user dashboard or room-list operation.
Fix: Add an index on hostId (e.g. @@index([hostId])) and deploy migration; consider indexes for other FK/filter columns (mapId, currentUsers) used in filters or ordering.

--- INFO ---

[DB-5] Fallback DB handlers mask connectivity failures (development-friendly)
File: src/lib/db.ts (fallback handler section, e.g., createFallbackHandler)
Evidence: When _isPrismaConnected is false, dbFallback returns mock objects/empty arrays instead of bubbling errors.
Usefulness: This is helpful for local dev but can hide production DB failures and create misleading behavior under partial outages; treat as implementation detail and keep it disabled in production.
